newsitem.title: GERMANY: Aluminium extrusions must fight to keep markets.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium extrusions must fight to keep markets.

text.p: Producers of aluminium extrusions could expect demand growth in developing countries but will have to support growth in the industrialised world, said Ivar Hafsett, president of Hydro Aluminium S.A.
"Costs to stay in business will increase," he said.
Many important integrated aluminium producers had moved into more profitable areas, mostly flat rolled aluminium products.
As a result, promotion of aluminium extrusions was left to the large independent players with the exception of Latin America, where integrated producers were gaining ground.
Flat rolled products accounted for roughly 50 percent of aluminium demand and cast and forged products for a combined 15 percent, leaving the remaining 35 percent to extrusions.

Global extrusion consumption in 1996 had risen to seven million tonnes from 6.76 million in 1995, mostly on the strength of building industry demand in the developing world. But the industrialised world still consumed 65 percent of total volumes.

Hafsett said the industry should move more aggressively into the automotive sector. Structural applications and heat transfer systems as well as aviation and shipping uses for lightweight extrusions also needed to be explored.
